+import asyncio
+import inspect
+
+import pytest
+
+from tenacity import RetryCallState, Retrying, retry_if_exception_cause_type
+from tenacity.retry import retry_all as SAll
+from tenacity.retry import retry_any as SAny
+from tenacity.asyncio.retry import retry_if_exception as AsyncException
+
+
+def policies():
+    trace = []
+    state = RetryCallState(Retrying(), fn=None, args=(), kwargs={})
+    error = RuntimeError("outer")
+    error.__cause__ = ValueError("cause")
+    state.set_exception((type(error), error, None))
+
+    class Cause(retry_if_exception_cause_type):
+        def __init__(self, label, exception_type):
+            super().__init__(exception_type)
+            self.label = label
+
+        def __call__(self, retry_state):
+            trace.append(self.label)
+            return super().__call__(retry_state)
+
+    def async_policy(label, value):
+        async def predicate(exception):
+            await asyncio.sleep(0)
+            trace.append(label)
+            return value
+        return AsyncException(predicate)
+
+    def plain(label, value):
+        def predicate(retry_state):
+            trace.append(label)
+            return value
+        return predicate
+
+    operands = {
+        "t": Cause("t", ValueError),
+        "f": Cause("f", KeyError),
+        "a": async_policy("a", False),
+        "b": async_policy("b", True),
+        "p": plain("p", False),
+        "q": plain("q", True),
+        "SAll": SAll,
+        "SAny": SAny,
+    }
+    return operands, state, trace
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "expression, expected, calls",
+    [
+        ("t & a", False, "t a"),
+        ("a & t", False, "a"),
+        ("f | b", True, "f b"),
+        ("b | f", True, "b"),
+        ("f & b", False, "f"),
+        ("b & f", False, "b f"),
+        ("t | a", True, "t"),
+        ("a | t", True, "a t"),
+        ("(t & b) | a", True, "t b"),
+        ("(f | a) & b", False, "f a"),
+        ("a | (t & b)", True, "a t b"),
+        ("b & (f | a)", False, "b f a"),
+        ("p | b", True, "p b"),
+        ("b & q", True, "b q"),
+        ("q & a", False, "q a"),
+        ("a | p", False, "a p"),
+        ("SAll(t, a) | f", False, "t a f"),
+        ("SAny(f, a) & t", False, "f a"),
+        ("SAll(t, b) & q", True, "t b q"),
+        ("p | SAny(f, b)", True, "p f b"),
+        ("SAny(f, SAll(t, a)) | b", True, "f t a b"),
+        ("(SAny(f, a) | f) & b", False, "f a f"),
+        ("t & SAny(f, a)", False, "t f a"),
+        ("SAll(t, a) | SAny(f, b)", True, "t a f b"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_mixed_expression(expression, expected, calls):
+    operands, state, trace = policies()
+    policy = eval(expression, {"__builtins__": {}}, operands)
+
+    async def run():
+        result = policy(state)
+        assert inspect.isawaitable(result)
+        assert await result is expected
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
+    assert trace == calls.split()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "expression, expected, calls",
+    [
+        ("t & q", True, "t q"),
+        ("f | p", False, "f p"),
+        ("SAny(f, p) & t", False, "f p"),
+        ("t | SAll(f, q)", True, "t"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_synchronous_expression_remains_synchronous(expression, expected, calls):
+    operands, state, trace = policies()
+    policy = eval(expression, {"__builtins__": {}}, operands)
+    assert policy(state) is expected
+    assert trace == calls.split()

spec.question:
Make mixed synchronous/asynchronous retry-policy composition reliable. Expressions using `&` and `|` with `tenacity.retry.retry_if_exception_cause_type` and `tenacity.asyncio.retry.retry_if_exception` must produce awaitable policies in either operand order. Evaluate operands left to right, await asynchronous predicates before using their boolean results, and short-circuit normally. Preserve parentheses and grouping across unlike operators.

This must also work when an operand is an existing synchronous `tenacity.retry.retry_any` or `retry_all` containing an asynchronous strategy, including recursively nested composites. Once such an operand participates in an operator expression, the whole expression must evaluate asynchronously without a synchronous inner composite treating a coroutine as truthy. Plain synchronous callable operands must work on either side, including when the asynchronous strategy is nested inside the other operand. Expressions containing only synchronous strategies and callables must retain their synchronous boolean behavior.

Return a unified diff against non-test repository files. Keep exception-chain traversal unchanged.

suggestion.behavior_shift: Cross-file dependency tracing replaces the original single-module direct solve. Reading both retry modules together is useful to follow forward and reflected operators and distinguish synchronous any/all evaluation from awaited evaluation. Focused execution probes can verify operand order and reveal unawaited coroutine results; delegation is not necessary.
suggestion.description: Repair mixed synchronous/asynchronous retry-policy composition. Use tenacity/retry.py::retry_if_exception_cause_type as a synchronous operand and tenacity/asyncio/retry.py::retry_if_exception as an asynchronous operand. Require both operand orders for & and | to produce awaitable composites that evaluate operands in source order, short-circuit correctly, and preserve grouping across unlike operators. Include nested expressions and plain synchronous callable operands. Return a unified diff against non-test files, targeting the operator dispatch in tenacity/retry.py::retry_base and tenacity/asyncio/retry.py::async_retry_base as needed; do not change exception-chain traversal.
suggestion.expected_answer_change: The patch must ensure that compositions containing asynchronous strategy objects use the asynchronous retry_any or retry_all implementation, including when a synchronous composite appears on the left. It must preserve ordered short-circuit evaluation and avoid flattening across unlike operators. Verification should use awaited predicates with invocation traces, including an async predicate returning false, rather than cause/context traversal tests.
suggestion.why_substantive: The problem moves from selecting exception links to selecting the correct composite implementation. In this snapshot, a synchronous strategy on the left can delegate to an asynchronous operand's reflected operator, whereas an asynchronous strategy on the left directly constructs an async composite. Nested synchronous composites can still consume coroutine results as truthy values rather than awaiting them. Correctness therefore depends on Python's operator dispatch and composite evaluation, not the accepted task's include_context option.
